findings.title: Silence action is rendered but cannot open its drawer for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
findings.body: The new list supplies only `promRule` for Grafana-managed rules. `AlertRuleMenu` now correctly enables “Silence notifications” from the Prometheus-rule ability, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. With no `rule`/ruler payload this condition is always false, so the visible silence menu item is a no-op.

findings.title: Delete is unavailable for Grafana rules in the ruler-free list
findings.body: For list entries loaded solely from the Grafana Prometheus endpoint, `canDelete` can be true through `grafanaDeleteAbility`, but the delete item additionally requires `rulerRule`. Since the new `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes no ruler rule, users with delete permission never receive a Delete action. The supplied `handleDelete` already closes over the identifier and does not require the ruler object, so this gate prevents an otherwise authorized operation.

findings.title: Pause capability from the Prometheus rule cannot produce a pause action
findings.body: `canPause` is calculated as an OR of ruler and Grafana Prometheus abilities, but the only rendered pause control still requires a Grafana ruler rule. In the new ruler-free Grafana list, a rule can be reported as pausable from its Prometheus representation while no Pause/Resume menu item is rendered, removing pause control from the list.

findings.title: Skip-token Grafana ability checks grant duplicate support to non-Grafana rules
findings.body: Passing `skipToken` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`. That path treats the missing rule as supported (`MaybeSupported` is `AlwaysSupported`) and returns Duplicate allowed based on Grafana rule-create permission. `AlertRuleMenu` invokes this path for non-Grafana Prometheus rules and ORs its result with the source-specific ability, so a user who can create Grafana rules but lacks permission to duplicate an external rule can still be shown the Duplicate action for that external rule. The skip-token path must return unsupported/denied abilities rather than evaluating Grafana permissions for an undefined rule.

findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: The previous combined-rule ability calculation could determine federation from the rule group. The refactor passes only the ruler rule and group identifier into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` and hard-codes `isFederated = false`. Consequently federated external rule groups can now receive update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent-delete capabilities when their permissions otherwise allow them, despite the prior explicit restriction for federated rules.

findings.title: Grafana rule list entries lost their React keys
findings.body: The Grafana branch maps over `rules` without assigning the computed `key` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, unlike the datasource and unknown branches and unlike the previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` rendering. React will reconcile these entries by position while pages are appended or updated, which can retain action/dropdown component state on the wrong rule and emits missing-key warnings. Pass `key={key}` to this component.
